regeln: Within each spoken phase use multiple distinct relevant shots, roughly 3-5 seconds each for Shorts; long videos can allow purposeful longer demonstrations. Preserve continuous narration and accurate subtitle timing.
A zoom, crop, subtitle change or decorative background does not count as a new motif. Never fill missing images with candles, unrelated stock or background-only frames.
Show the main image prominently; avoid tiny repeated photos in a mostly empty vertical frame. Preserve genuine evidence and important image details.
For AI Tools Explained identify the exact tool briefly, then show genuine interface views and different source-supported examples. Never present stock or an illustration as a real tool result.
Use original urban painted open-world-game poster styling for fictional scenes and presenters; no copied game characters. Match narrated action and era.

Clear speech and readable captions alone do not make a professional video. Inspect useful motif changes and narration-image alignment over the entire video. Missing main imagery is a substantial defect.
Include mandatory spoken like, share and save calls at the correct format-specific positions. Do not replace this requirement with a different CTA.

AI Tools Explained is for viewers with a practical task. Do not read parameter counts, architecture names, pipeline tags, context lengths or benchmark claims as a substitute for useful explanation. Explain the human task, the source-supported action and a concrete limit. A generic trending-tools question failed story review twice; prefer a specific visual workflow.

The user confirmed original presenter references on 2026-10-05: Business Origin Stories uses the blue-eyed man with a fedora, grey suit, dark tie and gold pocket watch; AI Tools Explained uses the black-haired man with black leather jacket and glowing cyan glasses. Preserve identity and typical clothing, vary action and setting.

Introduce the correct presenter at the opening and bring that same presenter back during the video in useful actions. Do not confine the figure to the ending. Do not replace original channel figures with different fictional people; anonymous period workers remain clearly illustrative supporting people, never a real-founder likeness.

Prefer vivid original painted open-world-game scenes to long holds on lifeless documentary photos. Preserve factual accuracy and show authentic tool examples briefly as evidence. Camera moves alone are not new motifs or full character animation.

The user confirmed on 2026-10-05 that both new delivered videos are much better than before. Preserve the original painted world, recurring channel identity, matching main imagery, music and useful scene changes. The long-term quality target remains 10/10; the user did not give these videos a numeric score. Do not replace their actual AI scores or the existing 7/10 delivery threshold with the aspirational target.

Prioritize genuine tool interfaces and outputs over abstract geometry, generic stock, or stylized illustrations during technical explanations.

Verify all technical claims, software versions, and pricing against sources; prioritize specific visual workflows over generic trending topics.

What are projects? | Claude Help Center
Note: A new version of projects is now available in beta, rolling out in stages starting with Claude Code. We've started moving existing projects for some Pro, Max, and Ultra users to the new version. See The new version of projects (beta) below.
Projects allow you to create self-contained workspaces with their own chat histories and knowledge bases. Within each project, you can upload documents, provide context, and have focused chats with Claude.
Projects are available to all users, including those with free Claude accounts. Free users can create a maximum of five projects.
The new version of projects (beta)
We're rolling out a new version of projects in stages, starting with Claude Code. In the new version, a project is one conversation: you say what you need as it comes to you, and Claude breaks the work into parallel threads that run in the cloud. Claude tells you what's done and what's waiting on you, and if you close your laptop, the threads keep going. Every thread starts with the project's files, repositories, instructions, and memory, and the project's Library collects the files you add and the files Claude produces.
The new version is now available in beta to select Pro, Max, and Ultra subscribers who use Claude Code, and to some Pro, Max, and Ultra users whose existing projects we’ve moved to the new version. If you have it, you'll see "Projects" in the sidebar at claude.ai/code and in the Code tab of the Claude desktop app. More Claude Code users on Pro, Max, and Ultra plans will get access as the rollout expands, and chat, Cowork, Team, and Enterprise will follow. If you're on Pro, Max, or Ultra plan and don't have access yet, you can join the waitlist .
We’ve started moving existing projects for some Pro, Max, and Ultra users to the new version. Nothing is lost or deleted in the move. Everything in your project comes with it: your instructions, files, full chat history, and scheduled tasks. You’ll pick up right where you left off. If you've used an existing project within the last 30 days, we’ll email you before we move your projects. Other existing projects in chat and Cowork stay on the current version for now, and we’ll move them as the rollout expands.
Projects draw from your plan's usage like any other use of Claude, and running several threads at once uses it faster.
For more on the new version, see Projects in the Claude Code docs. The rest of this article describes the current version of projects.
A key benefit of projects is the ability to provide context for your chats with Claude. You can upload relevant documents, text, code, or other files to a project's knowledge base, which Claude will use to better understand the context and background for your individual chats within that project.
In addition, you can define project instructions for each project to further tailor Claude's responses. For example, instructing Claude to use a more formal tone or answer questions from the perspective of a specific role or industry.
Enhanced project knowledge with RAG is only available to users with paid Claude plans (Pro, Max, Ultra, Team, or Enterprise).
When using a paid plan, your projects automatically scale to handle large amounts of content through Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG). When your project knowledge approaches context limits, Claude seamlessly enables RAG mode to expand capacity by up to 10x while maintaining response quality.
For more information on leveraging expanded project knowledge capacity, see Retrieval augmented generation (RAG) for projects .
Collaboration and sharing (Team and Enterprise plans only)
For users on Team and Enterprise plans, projects can be shared with other members of your organization, enabling powerful collaboration and knowledge sharing capabilities. The sharing system includes:
Can view: Members can see project contents, knowledge, and instructions, and chat within the project, but cannot edit it.
Can edit: Members can modify project instructions and knowledge, add/remove members, update member settings, and actively contribute to the project.
Share to specific members instead of making a project fully private or public to the entire organization.
Make a previously-created private project visible to the whole organization.
Individual sharing: Share projects with specific team members by email.
Bulk sharing: Add multiple users at once using email lists.
Organization-wide sharing: Make projects available to everyone in your organization either when creating the project or afterward.
Note: If an Owner or Primary Owner disables public projects, organization-wide sharing will be disabled both when creating the project and afterward.
Admin controls: Owners can turn off project sharing for your organization, or on Enterprise plans for specific roles. Turning off Share projects also turns off Public projects . When sharing is off, users can't share projects with new users or groups, and existing shares stay in place.
Shared with me tab: Easily find projects that others have shared with you.
Email notifications: Get notified when someone shares a project with you.
Access management: Project creators can modify permissions or remove access as needed.
Multiple members can contribute documents, create chats, and work together within the same project environment, making projects ideal for team collaboration.
For more information on getting started with projects, see How can I create and manage projects?
For more information on private projects and visibility settings on Team and Enterprise plans, see Project visibility and sharing .

belege.name: Wild Horse Nine
belege.text:
Wild Horse Nine is a 2026 black comedy  film written and directed by Martin McDonagh. A co-production of the United Kingdom, United States, and Chile, it stars John Malkovich, Sam Rockwell, Steve Buscemi, Mariana di Girolamo, Ailín Salas, Tom Waits, and Parker Posey. The film follows two CIA officers in 1973 who travel to Easter Island for an assignment and wrestle with their dark pasts.
Wild Horse Nine premiered in the main competition of the 83rd Venice International Film Festival on 3 September 2026, where Malkovich won the Volpi Cup for Best Actor. It was widely released by Searchlight Pictures on November 6. The film received positive reviews from critics.


== Plot ==
In 1973, CIA officers Chris Carlisle and Lee Chesterfield vacation to Easter Island from their station in Santiago, Chile. At the airport, they encounter Monica and Alicia, two young left-wing students. Chris jokes to them that they are CIA agents there to destabilize their government, which is quickly brushed aside by Lee.
During their trip, Chris's crude behavior and morphine addiction is of constant annoyance to Lee, though it is mostly tolerated. Chris is aging and has begun recording a memoir on his voice recorder of his various involvements during his career (including the Guatemalan coup d'etat, the Bay of Pigs invasion, the assassination of Patrice Lumumba and the Kennedy assassination, among others). However, this is opposed by bureau chief MJ, who, it is later revealed, has instructed Lee to kill Chris lest he reveal confidential information.
The pair travel to various destinations on the island. It is revealed that Chris has dementia and terminal cancer with a week to live; he has asked Lee to kill him at the end of their trip, though he himself no longer remembers this fact. Chris believes that they are being followed and becomes increasingly paranoid and volatile. When Lee tries to confirm their plans with Chris, a confused Chris responds that he would rather visit Venice and insists that Lee books a new itinerary. A frustrated Lee relents.
Meanwhile, MJ pressures Lee, who is torn between his duty and his loyalty to Chris, to tie up loose ends. He needs Lee to locate a rifle which was used to assassinate Kennedy. Lee finds their hotel receptionist rummaging through Chris's belongings and discovers that she is acting on instructions from MJ. MJ coerces Lee by kidnapping his wife and children, and decides to travel to Easter Island himself.
Chris meets Monica again and apologizes for his earlier remarks. In the evening, while attending a Victor Jara concert, he informs her that Chilean president Salvador Allende will be overthrown and activists like her and Alicia will be persecuted. He warns her to flee and advises her to never stop fighting if she is being made to get into a car, but she angrily rebuffs him. Whilst leaving, Chris realizes that Monica's car had been the one following him.
MJ arrives on the island, and Lee goes alone to meet him. He pleads with MJ to spare Chris and let them go in peace to Venice. However, MJ refuses and insists Chris is to be killed on the island. MJ, Alicia (a CIA mole who was working for MJ all along), and Lee head to find Chris, who has forced Monica at gunpoint to drive him away from the hotel. After confirming that she is not a spy, he advises her on how to possibly prevent the upcoming Chilean regime, telling her to kill any person she sees in uniform, while acknowledging that even then there will be more people; the regime is inevitable. Still, this sparks a spirit of resistance in Monica.   
As Monica drives away, she is stopped by MJ. As his men drag Monica towards a car, she struggles to resist them with all her might until they are shot dead by Chris with the rifle used to kill Kennedy. She escapes after running over Alicia. MJ orders Lee to kill Chris, but Lee, disillusioned, shoots MJ instead. Lee and Chris share one final conversation, during which Chris gives Lee a film reel of the Kennedy assassination to be used as leverage to save Lee's family. Chris finally gives Lee the code word to kill him, which he does. In his final voice recording, Chris briefly reflects that he "could have killed a lot less people" and "should've hung out with a lot more horses".


== Cast ==
John Malkovich as Chris Carlisle, a veteran CIA officer with terminal cancer and Lee's mentor
Sam Rockwell as Lee Chesterfield, a CIA officer and Chris's protégé
Steve Buscemi as MJ, a CIA bureau chief stationed in Chile and Chris and Lee's boss
Mariana di Girolamo as Monica, a Chilean college student Chris befriends and Alicia's friend
Ailín Salas as Alicia, Monica's travel companion
Tom Waits as Jim Carlisle, Chris's brother
Parker Posey as Marge Chesterfield, Lee's wife
Paola Giannini as Rosa, hotel receptionist


== Production ==
McDonagh has said that he first learned about the 1973 Chilean coup, and the torture and murder of detainees at Estadio Chile – events referenced throughout the film – in The Clash’s song "Washington Bullets", from their 1980 album Sandinista!.
In February 2025, it was reported that a film written and directed by Martin McDonagh was in development for Searchlight Pictures with Blueprint Pictures and Film4 co-producing and Taylor Friedman and Peter Spencer overseeing the project. It would be produced by Graham Broadbent, Pete Czernin, and Anita Overland. The film was set to star Sam Rockwell, John Malkovich, and Mark Ruffalo. The same month, Parker Posey joined the cast. In March 2025, Steve Buscemi joined the cast, replacing Ruffalo after he left the project. Mariana di Girolamo, Tom Waits, Ailín Salas, and Paola Giannini are also part of the cast. Ben Davis was announced as the film's cinematographer.
Principal photography began that month, on Rapa Nui, and then, in April, continued at a rayuela club in Conchalí, the Arturo Merino Benítez International Airport, and the center of Santiago city. Filming wrapped on 28 April.


=== Music ===


== Release ==

The film had its world premiere in the main competition of the 83rd Venice International Film Festival on 3 September 2026. It had its North American premiere at the 53rd Telluride Film Festival. It was also programmed in the 'Perlak' sidebar section of the 74th San Sebastián International Film Festival. It screened in the Gala section of 39th Tokyo International Film Festival on 2 November 2026. It also screened at the 15th Montclair Film Festival as the opening night film on October 16th. It opened the 2026 Stockholm International Film Festival on November 11, 2026.
It was released theatrically on 6 November 2026 by Searchlight Pictures.


== Reception ==


=== Box office ===
Wild Horse Nine has grossed $40 million worldwide. It has grossed $19 million in North America.

Age assurance on Claude | Claude Help Center
Claude, our consumer product, is only available to people over 18 years. You’ll need to confirm you’re 18 or over while setting up an account. When we detect signals that you may be under 18, we'll ask you to verify your age before you can continue using Claude.
We have safety systems in place to detect if people under 18 may be using Claude and we’ll disable accounts based on indicators of minor activity.
You’ll have the option to verify your age using one of our third-party age verification providers, Yoti or Persona. A link for verification will be provided in the notification email. If you pass the age verification process, your account will be reinstated.
There are several ways to confirm you're 18 or over. Available options may vary:
Facial age estimation: Take a selfie and the provider’s technology estimates your age. No ID document needed to start. You may be asked for an ID if more information is needed.
ID verification: Take a photo of your ID (such as a passport, driving license, or national ID card) and upload it from your device. Accepted IDs vary by country and provider. If you're verifying with Yoti, see their full list of supported documents .
Yoti’s Digital ID app: If you already have the Yoti app, share a verified "over 18" attribute from it.
Yoti and Persona are independently audited age verification providers for SOC2 compliance. Your selfie, document images, and any biometric information are deleted by the provider after your age is checked. Anthropic doesn't store your ID or image. We keep the result of the check and details about it, which can include the method used.

belege.name: Claude Wild
belege.text:
Claude Wild (born 1 March 1964 in Lausanne) is a Swiss diplomat.


== Life ==


=== Education ===
Claude Wild studied political science and international relations at the Graduate Institute of International Studies in Geneva where he completed a postgraduate degree.


=== Diplomatic career ===
He was appointed ambassador and head of the Human Security Department of the Federal Department of Foreign Affairs in 2010. In 2015, Ambassador Wild became Switzerland's permanent representative to the Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), the United Nations, and other international organizations in Vienna.
Wild became ambassador to Kyiv in 2019 and was ambassador to Ukraine in the first months of the Russo-Ukrainian war. In early March 2022, Wild and his staff had to be escorted out of the country by special forces due to the threatening security situation. He returned to his post in the Ukrainian capital in May 2022. Wild was subsequently made responsible for the implementation of Swiss aid in Ukraine. He has repeatedly clarified that Switzerland's principle of neutrality in foreign policy (so-called Swiss neutrality) means, in the context of the war, that the country “does not join a military alliance, and does not send weapons to the conflict zone, even to support the victims”, yet “we stand clearly behind the Ukrainian position.” He has warned against Switzerland adopting a stance of "neutrality fetishism" in the context of the war. His posting as ambassador to Ukraine ended at the end of March 2023, and he was succeeded by Félix Baumann.
In April 2023, Wild became the permanent representative of Switzerland to the Council of Europe.
